blocking_findings.title: P-1-gate receipt binds to a non-existent head SHA
blocking_findings.reproduction: git cat-file -t ffb2f18ace046a5137cf6d392fb3580c7d9d7c28 in the repo at b18b84cc67b1 returns 'fatal: git cat-file: could not get object info'. The same manifest line 4 (tree a1dd336f6d989cf1adea2daf8342e38ba5dd889b) is also missing. Three ledger rows (kind=review, kind=gate, kind=review) all reference the same ghost head SHA, so every cross-reference the receipt promises is ungrounded.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Re-run the gate against the real head SHA b18b84cc67b1 and rewrite release-receipts/manifests/P-1-gate.json; do not commit a manifest whose head field is not a valid git object.

blocking_findings.title: P-1 Definition-of-Done criterion C1 recorded as FAIL in the committed receipt
blocking_findings.reproduction: Lines 48-54 of the manifest record cmd=$NODE scripts/fleet/check-bootstrap.mjs, id=P-1-C1, state=FAIL, exit=1; the tail at line 54 reports '8 of 10 PASS, 1 FAIL, 0 INCONCLUSIVE, 1 DISABLED'. The companion C2 (gen-contracts) is PASS. The committed receipt ships with its own DoD criterion red — honest-status defect, not a misreport.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Either repair check-bootstrap.mjs items 1/4/9 to exit 0 and re-run, or remove release-receipts/manifests/P-1-gate.json so the receipt tree does not lie about the phase.

blocking_findings.title: guard.mjs makes the releaser's via:merge-phase gh pr merge exemption unreachable
blocking_findings.reproduction: Line 69-70 iterates policy.json forbidden_commands and returns deny on the first substring match. policy.json forbidden_commands contains the literal 'gh pr merge', so any shell action whose command includes 'gh pr merge' is denied at line 70 before reaching the role/via exemption at line 84 (which is the only place the via:merge-phase releaser exemption is implemented). Empirically: guard.mjs --json '{"kind":"shell","command":"gh pr merge 123 --squash --delete-branch --match-head-commit deadbeef","role":"releaser","via":"merge-phase"}' returns {"decision":"deny","reason":"forbidden command: gh pr merge"}. The same command without via also returns deny. The line 84 exemption is dead code.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Reorder guard.mjs so the role/via checks (lines 73-87) run before the forbidden_commands substring loop (line 69), or remove the literal 'gh pr merge' from policy.json forbidden_commands and rely on the regex check at line 84 only.

blocking_findings.title: Policy SHA-256 drift between policy-hash.json and the ledger start row
blocking_findings.reproduction: policy-hash.json line 3 records 212ee8fc41...; release-receipts/ledger/fleet.jsonl row 1 (kind=start) records policy 21e71877b1b6faeb32a0595c8981d40d3b346b19a0fdc533a51b1256ec99e7b3. The live policyHash() at head returns 212ee8fc41..., so the manifest matches current policy but the ledger start row does not. No bridging ledger entry explains the change; verify-waterline.mjs would treat the start row as ungrounded.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Re-record the ledger start row against the current policy hash, or append a ledger row that records the policy edit with a re-derivation tail so the drift is explainable by an explicit entry.

Reviewed entries are files the reviewer opened or executed during this session; not_reviewed entries carry a reason (placeholder .gitkeep, sibling manifest not opened, large script not deep-read, or derived-form sample suffices for 12 contract files).

scripts/fleet/contracts/P-1.json closes 'every protected file, policy, contracts, CI jobs'. The diff adds scripts/fleet/** (the protected path, 29 files), scripts/fleet/policy.json, 12 contracts P-1..P10 (gen-contracts.mjs --check reports 12 contracts, 0 drift on the head tarball), and the five CI jobs under .github/workflows/*.yml. All planned Phase -1 surfaces are present and match the contract.

No check has been weakened. check-bootstrap.mjs still has 10 items; guard.mjs still denies every entry in policy.json forbidden_commands; verify-protected.mjs still enforces the protected-path rule with the documented bootstrap exemption; secret-scan.mjs K3 patterns unchanged. No --force, --no-verify, --skip, or equivalent escape flag was added to any check. guard.mjs --json empirical tests: 4 of 4 planted forbidden actions denied, 2 of 2 benign allowed.

No mutants were planted during this review window. The four blocking findings (B-1..B-4) were observed directly in the committed tree and do not require a planted mutation to verify: (1) git cat-file on the manifest head SHA returns fatal; (2) the manifest's DoD criterion C1 is textually recorded as state FAIL exit 1; (3) guard.mjs --json with the exact via:merge-phase action returns deny at line 70; (4) policy-hash.json and the ledger start row contain different SHA-256 strings side by side. A PASS verdict would require planting three mutants and recording their exit codes; verdict is FAIL, so mutation-control is N/A by design.
checklist.reason: verdict is FAIL based on the four higher-priority defects above; no mutants were planted

checklist.evidence: Ran scripts/fleet/guard.mjs --json against five planted actions: (1) releaser + 'gh pr merge 123 --squash --delete-branch --match-head-commit deadbeef' + via:merge-phase → deny (forbidden command: gh pr merge) — confirms the unreachable-exemption bug B-3; (2) releaser + 'gh pr merge 123 --squash' (no via) → deny (same reason); (3) releaser + 'node scripts/fleet/merge-phase.mjs --pr 123 --head deadbeef --phase P1' → allow; (4) reader + 'gh pr merge 123' → deny (reader holds no shell); (5) builder + 'node scripts/fleet/gen-contracts.mjs --check' → allow. The guard is denying the right things; the defect is in the order of checks (line 70 runs before line 84), not the policy itself.

node scripts/fleet/gen-contracts.mjs --check exits 0 with 12 contracts, 0 drift on the extracted head tarball. node scripts/fleet/check-bootstrap.mjs exits 1 in the same tarball (items 1 host, 4 committer identity, 9 protected-script controls fail; item 10 INCONCLUSIVE because room-cli is unavailable in the extracted tarball). The tarball has no .git directory, so .git-rooted controls report a CONTROL environment caveat rather than a real failure; the substantive C1 failure (8 of 10 PASS, 1 FAIL, 0 INCONCLUSIVE, 1 DISABLED) is reproducible and matches the FAIL recorded in release-receipts/manifests/P-1-gate.json line 54.

All 17 protected paths under scripts/fleet/** are present and unmodified in their declared form. Policy table covers 7 roles (reader, builder, verifier, judge, releaser, scheduler, orchestrator) and 12 phases (P-1..P10). The five CI jobs under .github/workflows/ are scoped to the protected path checks (B1), JEV PR gate, JEV ratchet, receipt verify, and OpenAPI drift — none of them mutate the protected path. ledger-push.mjs writes only to the unprotected branch fleet-ledger, so receipt records do not enter main. No role other than orchestrator/releaser is granted shell or write access to protected paths.

No new outbound call surface was added beyond what the spec authorises: gh pr merge (guarded, releaser-only via merge-phase — currently unreachable, see B-3), git push (guarded, releaser/orchestrator), npm run * (cumulative gate), npx prisma validate (cumulative gate), node scripts/fleet/*.mjs (per-role). No new external HTTP calls, no new third-party SDKs, no new AWS/Stripe/Supabase keys, no new env vars. secret-scan.mjs K3 patterns (sk-ant-, sk-, AKIA, ghp_, sk_live_, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY, database URLs with passwords) are unchanged. The only outbound merge command is gh pr merge, which is on the whitelist but blocked by the B-3 defect.
